Hi Max / team —

Answers inline:
1) Streaming partials: Redwood supports chunked JSON streaming. Best practice is to emit newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) or an open-array pattern with delimiter tokens so clients can process items incrementally. We avoid sending half-closed JSON objects; instead, each event is a standalone JSON object sent as a stream item. That keeps parsing robust across reconnects.

2) Tool response shape: function/tool payloads can include nested arrays/objects. Practical constraints: payloads > 16KB may trigger streaming the tool response in chunks; we recommend keeping individual retrieval metadata objects under ~2–3KB and limit nested depth to 4 levels to avoid client memory spikes when rehydrating. We will surface retrieval metadata fields: source_id, score, highlights (array), and truncated_text.

3) Token cost estimate (very rough back-of-envelope):
- Model context cost: user prompt (300 tokens) + retrieval (600 tokens) + 6 events * 120 tokens = 300 + 600 + 720 = 1,620 tokens per session.
- With Redwood hosted pricing tier X: estimated ~1.62k tokens * $0.0006/token = ~$0.97 per session (note: exact pricing depends on model & quantization; we'll run a small benchmark).

Operational notes:
- For 95th percentile latency <400ms we recommend: use prefix/KV caching for the retrievals, enable batch size=8 for throughput tests, and pin the model to a low-latency variant in the US region. Marcus will share a short runbook pre-kickoff.

Link to engineering brief: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C4D-pulseai-onboarding (see /Tech/runbooks/partial-streaming.md)
